title: Seeing Stars
program_note:
1.  Solar Flares. On the roiling surface of the sun, spots gather and become brighter, from which eruptions small and large violently emanate.  Prominences of gas and light develop and elongate, ultimately dissipating and disappearing back into the surface of the sun.

2.  Night Stars. Quiet but sparkling and shining points of light and sound coalesce into gently defined lines, at times sparse, at times intricate and detailed.

III.   Seeing Stars.  The mental image of stars falling and dissipating after a violent explosion — or after a blow to the head.

The total duration of Seeing Stars is approximately 13:30, with the individual movements approximately 5:00, 5:15, and 3:10.

Seeing Stars is dedicated to Thomas Lee and the UCLA Wind Ensemble.

David S. Lefkowitz

Los Angeles, California

4 February, 1998
